english.title: Child abduction - parent send child out of UK
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person connected with **(..SPECIFY NAME..), a child under the age of 16, sent the said child out of the United Kingdom without the appropriate consent
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1) and 4 of the Child Abduction Act 1984.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being a parent/person connected with
a child under the age of 16
sent that child
out of the United Kingdom
without the appropriate consent

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See offence wording: H2066 - where the child is taken out of the UK by parent/person connected with the child.
(ii) See similar offence wordings: H2067 and H2075 where the child is taken/detained
from a person entitled to lawful control.
(iii) See other offence wordings: H1650, H2065, H2299, H2086, H2295, H2296, H2297 and H2300 where the child is taken/detained from a person entitled to lawful custody, taken/detained from custody of person with lawful control, taken/kept while in care or incited to run away.
(iv)See section 2(2) for person to whom this offence does not apply.
(v) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required before proceedings may commence.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
